previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: James, a 60-year-old man with a history of COPD, chronic alcohol dependence, and tobacco use, was readmitted one day after leaving a prior hospitalization against medical advice. He presented with shortness of breath and acute intoxication. He was treated for COPD exacerbation with prednisone, azithromycin, and bronchodilators, and his oxygen levels improved to the mid-90s on room air. His right middle lobe collapse remained unchanged on chest X-ray. He received diazepam for alcohol withdrawal and was encouraged to attend AA. Hypertension was managed with amlodipine. He was discharged home with a short-term oxycodone prescription for his right olecranon fracture pain, instructions to follow up with orthopedics and physical therapy, and a nicotine patch prescription to aid smoking cessation. He left with improved respiratory status and a plan for outpatient care.
problems: Acute alcoholic intoxication in alcoholism, unspecified
Closed fracture of olecranon process of ulna

Brief Hospital Course:
BRIEF HOSPITAL COURSE
=====================
___ year old gentleman with h/o depression, COPD, alcohol abuse 
with many recent hospital admissions who is admitted for alcohol 
withdrawal and ?PNA vs COPD exacerbation. He will undergo R

ACTIVE ISSUES
==============
# Dyspnea & cough: Patient has a history of COPD and multiple 
admissions for PNA in the past. Active smoker. In the ED he 
reported a new cough and difficulty breathing which was similar 
to prior episodes of PNA (treated for CAP in ___ and ___ so he was empirically started on levofloxacin. In the ED

continued on albuterol and ipratroprium nebs and started on 
flovent.

# Alcohol withdrawal: Patient has history of of DTs. Reports 
drinking ___ pints of whiskey per day. Elevated LFTs and 
thrombocytopenia were consisent with alcohol abuse. He received 
15mg of valium and banana bag in ED. On the floor he was 
continuned on a CIWA scale.  Social Work attempted to contact 
the patient but he did not want to speak to anyone at the time. 
He intermittently reported wanting to quit alcohol to his RN. 
However, he stated clearly several times that if we did not 
prescribe him methadone he would go across the street to the 
liquor store and begin drinking alcohol (reports that he drinks 
to numb pain in his elbow).

# Depression & ?SI: At arrival to ED the patient reported SI -- 
however at this time he was acutely intoxicated. Later when 
evaluated by Psychiatry in the ED he was noted to no longer have 
plans for suicide attempt. Psychiatry recommended that the 
patient does not need 1:1 sitter. He needs close psychiatric 
followup and would benefit from dual diagnosis treatment in the 
future.

# H/o right olecranon fracture: Followed by Dr. ___. Has 
missed follow up appointments and outpatient surgery. Ortho 
recommended repeat elbow imaging which showed continued 
fracture. They attempted to add him on to the OR schedule but he 
became upset that he had to wait too long and refused the 
procedure after getting a nerve block. He was brought back to 
his room. They then added him to next AM schedule, but he 
reported somebody told him he was no longer NPO and drank coffee 
with cream the morning of the procedure. Due to OR schedule he 
was not able to be scheduled again that day. He was given number 
for ___ clinic to follow up for outpatient surgery.

# Chronic pain: Pain ___ to orthopedic injuries and being 
dragged several hundred under a car by a lady on her cell phone. 
He also reported a recent fight during which he was hit in the 
face. This was corroborated by a PA who knows him well and 
reported that he regularly gets in fights at the ___. He 
was managed with oxycodone and acetaminophen in house. He was 
given a prescription for this as well until follow up. 

# Facial asymmetry: He noted being punched in the face at a bar 
recently. The left side of his face appears misshapen and 
sunken/asymmetric. He underwent CT sinus to evaluate for new 
fracture. This study showed that all changes were chronic and 
was negative for acute fracture/change.
